event: Day 37: the stone sings its full thirty-second dawn greeting again.
The bond network is at rest; the ghost-elms' shimmer reaches past its pre-pulse radius.
She writes a three-page list of fourteen tasks, enough to fill eighteen days.
Her mother's letter warns her not to turn being needed into a project; she closes the list.
At breakfast Hadley says they have ten days of food, fourteen if he forages.
He plans a two-day ridgeline run to the basin cache; Theron says 'Not alone.'
Hadley has walked it alone thirty times; he will leave tomorrow after Maret's planting.
Maret brought food for three days and has been here five.
'Plant first. Eat later.' Her grandmother planted during a famine.
'The ground does not wait for you to be comfortable.' Hadley yields and recalculates.
At the gap Wren finds the retreated strip: neither grey corrupted soil nor healthy ground.
Palm on it, she feels the corruption gone but the soil leached, rootless, waiting.
The strip lies unprotected between the old boundary and the new.
She journals the strip, about three meters wide: 'The ground is not corrupt. It is empty.'
A discovery logs the corruption retreat zone as unclaimed ground: +58 XP, 1999 / 2573.
She finds Theron standing still in the drainage channel's southern extension.
In the newly cleared strip the channel bends east and meets another channel.
A buried dressed-stone junction box splits the water; the east branch runs into corruption.
His father cleared the main channel every spring and never came this far: it was in the gap.
One more degree of retreat might clear the eastern channel entirely.
His grandmother never mentioned a branch; maybe there was no point knowing of dead ground.
'We will clear it. When the strip is stable. We will find where it goes.'
Brecca is on her fourth pass of the hall; the stone feels steadier, warm like hands.
At the north wall Brecca presses wet clay into a joint with her full weight.
Wren asks to try something, and lays Detail Notation on Brecca's fresh joint.
The mark sinks into a warm, intentional, non-geological signature.
'You are not repointing. The stone is holding your attention, and keeping it.'
'I am pressing clay into joints.' 'Not like this. The stone is listening to you.'
Brecca looks at her clay-grey hands; the retaining wall settles around her joints.
The System assigns Brecca the class [Stonekeeper], with no prior holders on record.
Her abilities are [Stone Listening] and [Pressed Intention]; she starts at Level 1.
Brecca reads it twice with shaking hands: 'Stonekeeper. Not Mason.'
'The System has never issued it before,' Wren says. 'Like Wayfinder.'
Brecca's envy since Millhaven rearranges into recognition.
'You saw it before the System did.' 'You were listening.' 'I was.'
A discovery logs the Stonekeeper manifestation site: +48 XP, 2047 / 2573.

changes.note: Discovery: Stonekeeper manifestation site, gathering hall

event: Wren does not look at the notification.
Maret chooses the western margin for the seedpods by pressing her hand to the earth.
'Why here?' Hadley asks. 'Because the ground said yes.'
They plant twelve: a thumb-width hollow, pod point-down, dust and silt, a palm pressed flat.
Her grandmother's survivors were the ones she talked to. 'I talk to everything.'
Brecca plants three, holding each pod a beat longer, her new class settling in her hands.
At the fire Wren writes a paragraph about Brecca's face, not the list.
Hadley has counted the chorus: thirty-two hours to return after pulse one, fourteen after two.
This time the high voices nearest the ghost-elms came back first.
The boundary insects came back third, not last: the boundary is healthier than the interior.
'You should write that down.' Hadley smiles: 'I did.'
Hadley goes to his bedroll; Brecca sleeps against the hall wall.
Maret counts notches by touch; Theron stands at the tree line looking south.
Wren rereads her Day 28 letter to her mother: all people, not one number.
She will give the letter to Hadley before his supply run.
She journals the full dawn song, the strip waiting for someone to plant, the junction.
She writes that Brecca is a Stonekeeper, and of the seedpods and Hadley's pattern.
She writes that she closed the fourteen-item list: some things just need someone to show up.
The chorus is full again. 'Two tomorrow.' She closes the journal without planning.
